name: Sihuas Ancash Quechua
world_status: statement found in a copy already on file

earlier_scan.source_named: Felix Quesada Castillo. 2013. Sihuas Quechua grammar sketch (15pp., per Glottolog); also SIL Peru materials by Diane & Daniel Hintz (sil.org blocked 403).

new_statements.quote: En la mayor parte de Ancash, del mismo modo que en virtualmente todas las variedades del quechua, la intensidad (acento) es más fuerte en la penúltima sílaba de cada palabra. La excepción más conspicua es el caso de las interjecciones, la mayoría de las cuales terminan en /w/ o /y/ y llevan una intensidad muy fuerte en la última sílaba. [...] En las provincias del Callejón de Huailas, el acento está en proceso de traslación hacia la sílaba inicial de la palabra.
new_statements.translation: In most of Ancash, as in virtually all varieties of Quechua, intensity (stress) is strongest on the penultimate syllable of each word. The most conspicuous exception is the case of interjections, most of which end in /w/ or /y/ and carry very strong intensity on the final syllable. [...] In the provinces of the Callejón de Huaylas, stress is in the process of shifting to the initial syllable of the word.
new_statements.citation: Parker, Gary J. 1976. Gramática quechua: Ancash-Huailas. Lima: Ministerio de Educación / Instituto de Estudios Peruanos. Sec. 2.4 'Acentuación', pp. 57-58.
new_statements.locator: sec. 2.4 Acentuación, p. 57 (first two sentences) and p. 58 (Callejón de Huaylas sentence); scope statement sec. 1.1 p. 25 and p. 26
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. Opened (187-page scan with scanned layer; Sec. 2.4 'Acentuación' begins on printed p. 57 (PDF p. 55) and continues on p. 58 (PDF p. 56). The quoted passage is there verbatim: 'En la mayor parte de Ancash, del mismo modo que en virtualmente todas las variedades del quechua, la intensidad (acento) es más fuerte en la penúltima sílaba de cada palabra. La excepción más conspicua es el caso de las interjecciones, la mayoría de las cuales terminan en /w/ o /y/ y llevan una intensidad muy fuerte en la última sílaba.' (p. 57) and 'En las provincias del Callejón de Huailas, el acento está en proceso de traslación hacia la sílaba inicial de la palabra.' (p. 58). Only scanned artefacts di…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the penultimate syllable of every word, throughout Ancash outside the Callejón de Huaylas (Sihuas is explicitly within the grammar's scope and is not in the Callejón). Corroborated by Hintz 2000 p.58 and p.116 fn.19, whose Ancash comparison set includes Sihuas (SH): initial stress occurs only in Corongo, Huaylas and Huaraz; all other varieties have basic penultimate stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not stated for Sihuas or for penult-stressing Ancash in general; Parker describes secondary/heavy-syllable effects only for the Callejón de Huaylas initial-stress system; Hintz 2000 fn.20 reports initial secondary stress for Huari (South Conchucos) after Stewart 1984.
new_statements.exceptions: Interjections ending in /w/ or /y/ are final-stressed (analysed as final long vowels); a small class of noun roots with a stressed final syllable (treated as closed final syllables with long vowels, sec. 2.3); Callejón de Huaylas varieties are shifting to initial stress; a final long syllable, esp. the 1st-person length /-:/, may attract stress (stated for Huaylas, p.60).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('cada palabra'); Parker notes intonation is unanalysed and treats the stress description as provisional. The statement is regional (most of Ancash), not a description of Sihuas specifically; the only Sihuas-specific description (Quesada 2013) is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is regional: Parker 1976 describes Ancash Quechua as a whole (his scope list p.25 names Sihuas province, and p.26 calls Sihuas the most conservative Ancash lect) and gives penultimate stress for 'most of Ancash', with the initial-stress innovation confined to the Callejón de Huaylas (huay1240). Hintz 2000 (Corongo, coro1247) independently restricts initial stress to Corongo, Huaylas and Huaraz, leaving Sihuas (SH, in his comparison set) penult-stressed. No source specific to Sihuas Quechua states stress: Quesada 2013, the only Sihuas-specific sketch, is silent. Parker's exception sentence about the Callejón de Huaylas does not apply to Sihuas. If the catalog requires a variety-specific first-hand statement, downgrade to accessible-description-silent-on-stress.

Sihuas is thus implicitly penult-stressed; stress is not listed as a row in the SH columns, so this is inference…
